Validated by compat/validate.py (CI) and the compat-matrix readiness gate. FSD/ONE_CLIENT_N_NODES.md §6.

Fixed (CIRISClient#2); against a node older than 0.5.188 nothing changes, because nothing emitted critical before it. (2) MODE: the agent surfaces are chosen at runtime from the probed ClientMode, now including the runtime's own data.role declaration. CIRISBuild.HAS_AGENT is DELETED (CIRISServer#479) — one build ships and narrows itself

rows.node_min_reason: unchanged from 0.5.188. The identity card's repair surface is additive and renders only when the node emits federation.key_subject_blind with a named subject (CIRISServer#490); a node that emits nothing shows nothing, which is the same screen 0.5.188 shipped
rows.capabilities_note: identity.repair is the CLIENT half of CIRISServer#490: a subject-blind federation key row (pre-CIRISPersist#659 envelope, naming only key_id) is refused at every peer it replicates to, and until now nothing told its owner. The card keys on Warning.code, never on Warning.message — which arrives already composed and never localized — and reads the subject from the structured subject_key_id (also accepting key_id, or key_id= on action_url). SEVERITY IS `warning` AND THE CARD IS RED ANYWAY: error would set degraded_mode, and this condition is permanent until repaired, so it would pin every node holding a stale row as degraded forever over something that degrades no service. Severity answers 'is this node degrading?'; prominence is keyed on the code. Scoped to the operator's own roster, so a stranger's malformed row cannot appear on it, and it renders NOTHING when no subject is named — fail-closed on both halves independently. LINEAGE SCOPING ('fedIDs descended from the portable ID') is NOT implemented: MintedIdentity carries no lineage field and the live damaged row has no delegates_to to walk (open question on CIRISServer#490). The roster relation is used instead, and the key_id string is never parsed for it

rows.capabilities_note: identity.federation_entry is the federation-ID-first login surface (CIRISAgent#887), and it arrives SHUT. This tree deliberately had no fedID sign-in option — the original vendor commit carried a note saying so by design, because a long-lived identity on the device is not proof of who is holding it, and entering on its presence alone is a second credential-less door beside the account login. That reasoning stands; the conclusion changes. Leaving the door out rather than shutting it meant the consumers, who HAVE this surface, would lose it on adoption — so the door is here and `mayEnterWithFederationIdentity` keeps it shut unless a real owner session is open. No per-fedID PIN: a second secret on the same door rebuilds the parallel-credential path this closes. The node agrees independently — resolve_user_signer will not sign with the fedID without the live owner session either

The wipe exists BECAUSE the authenticated reset (POST /v1/system/data/reset-account) is AuthAdminDep-gated and so unreachable from the login screen, which is where it is needed
rows.capabilities_note: inherited from CIRISAgent so that repo can delete client/ (CIRISClient#7, CIRISServer#495/#496): the published artifact was missing work that existed only there, and deleting client/ would have dropped it silently — CIRISAgent#1091's drift pointing the other way. diagnostics.export is a bundle plus log buffer on the three screens that can strand a user, Download and Copy both offered because they fail differently; gated to desktop and mobile, because on web the buffer is deliberately empty and on managed deployments the person at the UI is not necessarily entitled to the node's environment. device.local_wipe makes 'Reset device' match its own dialog: it NEVER deletes the home directory, only the entries the node generates, with tracked source skipped in a checkout and .git a veto — the fourth shape of that function, after three revisions each of which found a new way to destroy the wrong thing. Also: testableWithHandler now registers elements on iOS as well as Android (the same modifier had been making controls clickable but invisible to /tree), and the desktop logger feeds DebugLogBuffer, which it never did — so the bundle's log section was empty on desktop for the whole process lifetime

rows.notes: FIRST CUT UNDER THE RANGE. CIRISServer 0.5.192 moves to ciris-client>=0.5.190,<0.6 (CIRISServer#497), so this ships without a paired server release — the point of the decoupling. isVersionMismatch compares against a floor instead of equality, which under a range would have nagged on every legitimately-mixed pair. node_max_tested stays 0.5.190: the 0.5.191 node was fetched and the four-corner walk was NOT run against it, because port 4243 was held by a live agent this session had no business stopping. An untested bound is a guess with a version number on it, so the tested one is recorded. 24 review findings across seven rounds are in the git history; two were the claim PIN reaching the debug bundle through StartupViewModel's per-line logging, and FailurePanel's GitHub-issue body never passing through redaction at all

rows.capabilities_note: registry.verify is the FIRST surface shipped ahead of its API. No released node serves /v1/registry/lookup, so on every install today it renders the unavailable path and says WHICH unavailable — that is the feature, not a placeholder. CapabilityWire is the wire contract for the whole ecosystem: CIRISServer#499 declares conferred scopes in src/conformance.rs, CIRISAgent is adding an agent-tier field on /v1/system/health, and this is the one reader, written to be quoted rather than reimplemented. Four wire shapes, four answers — absent means an older peer, null means it could not read its own record, [] means it holds nothing, a list means membership — because those are four remedies and collapsing any pair produces a confident wrong answer instead of a missing one

rows.notes: The pattern cut: UI ahead of the API, gated on a declaration rather than probed for. CIRISServer shipped the declaration independently and drew the same null-versus-empty line in its own field docs, which is the useful signal — the distinction is a property of the problem, not a preference. Sixteen review findings landed on this branch and every one was the same shape: presenting an answer that was not there. A verdict from another node, a record for another hash, a transport failure read as an old node, the operator's own input echoed back as confirmation. The gate was sound from the first commit; the plumbing around attribution was where all the work was

rows.notes: THE GATE WAS ANSWERING A QUESTION THE WIZARD WAS NOT ASKING. clientMode decides whether AGENT-only surfaces and pollers run, and it demotes a folded-but-unconfigured brain to NODE (CIRISAgent#1075) because such a brain 503s every agent poller — the arm's own comment lists `addLlmProvider 503 <- so the user could not configure an escape`. The wizard then used that verdict to skip the step that calls addLlmProvider, so: unconfigured -> NODE -> no AI step -> still unconfigured. The fix that stopped the 503s had become the reason configuration never happened. ModeProbe.brainPresent = folded && reachable, independent of readiness, because readiness must not gate the step that produces it; the poller gate is unchanged. The provisional half is fixed too — setupHasAgent was `clientMode?.isAgent ?: false`, collapsing 'not probed yet' into 'no brain' while SetupViewModel is keyed on it, so Screen.Setup now waits for the probe rather than fixing its step list on a default. Third place this repo has needed distinct zeroes, after ModeProbe.undetermined and CapabilityWire's null-versus-empty

rows.notes: A CONTROL THAT COULD NEVER DO ANYTHING (CIRISClient#23). The login screen offered "Sign in as <key_id>" whenever the node reported a key_id — which on a fresh install is just the bootstrap keystore alias, so the button appeared for users who had no federation identity at all. It could not work even when it appeared: getOwnerHint resolves to null pre-setup one line above the render, and the click handler refused every press without a live owner session. The call site carried a comment stating there was deliberately NO fedID sign-in option here because a credential-less door was a security hole, and the button rendered twelve lines below it. The guard was correct and the door should not have been reopened behind it; both are now gone, along with mayEnterWithFederationIdentity, which existed only to keep it shut. Removed rather than relabelled: a control whose every outcome is a refusal has no name that makes it honest

rows.notes: TWO ARTIFACTS THAT LOOKED RIGHT AND WERE NOT. #25: an Android AAR never contains its project dependencies' classes — Gradle expects a consumer to resolve them from a repository via the POM beside it. This one is published as a bare file and dropped into apps/android/libs/, so there is no POM and no repository, and implementation(project(":generated-api")) could never reach a consumer. 0.5.195 shipped 5,820 ai/ciris/mobile classes and zero ai/ciris/api; every APK built against it died in onCreate with NoClassDefFoundError on AgentApi, from CIRISApiClient's constructor on the startup path. The AAR is now fat, and packaging/check_aar.py opens the artifact about to be uploaded and looks for the class the crash named — the broken release was a BUILD SUCCESSFUL producing a 16 MB file, so neither exit code nor size distinguished it. #26: LOCAL_NODE_URL was a const val naming :4243 at ~30 federation call sites while the app honoured CIRIS_NODE_URL everywhere else, so a desktop client attached to :4343 sent all twelve ordinary calls there and then minted the owner's federation identity on a node the operator had never attached to. The constant's own doc was right about WHY it exists and wrong that it could be constant: which node runs in-process is precisely what a compile-time value cannot know, and Main.kt already resolves it. Now set once by each platform entry point, which fixes all thirty sites without depending on having found them

rows.notes: THE MACHINERY WAS BUILT IN 0.5.196 AND NOTHING READ IT. BackendSupervisor shipped wired to lifecycle on three platforms with 18 tests, and no screen consumed its state, so a user with a dead backend still read "Cannot connect to server. Please check your connection." from an app whose backend runs inside itself — then restarted their phone and asked why Google sign-in had broken, because an unreachable backend surfaces on the login screen. noticeFor() is now an exhaustive `when` over BackendState with no else, so a new state cannot be added without deciding what the user is told and what they can do; verified by adding one and watching the build fail. Three properties are pinned by test: no state is silent, no broken state is a dead end, and "check your connection" appears only on Unreachable, where we could not ASK. The service's startup exception — previously written to a notification and dropped — now reaches GaveUp and the screen. DRIVABILITY IS AN INVARIANT: 61 btn_* tags had no handler and 124 input_* had no sink while /input answered success:true regardless, so /tree now carries canClick/canInput, /undrivable lists what is tagged-but-not-drivable per screen, and a baselined static check fails on new offenders. THE APP IS NOW STARTED BY CI, four times, against the four node configurations a universal client must serve (#10) — every defect this repo shipped previously lived past a green build because nothing ran the app. iOS Swift is type-checked against the real Kotlin framework for the first time (#24), which found a genuine captured-var race in the StoreKit transaction listener on first contact; fixed rather than accommodated by loosening the gate. Chat transcript tagged so automation can assert agent replies (#27). checkLlmConfig logs every path including success (#28).

rows.notes: REGRESSION FIX FOR 0.5.197 (CIRISClient#30). That cut made /input refuse with 422 when no text sink is registered — the right rule, since before it answered success:true after a fixed delay whether or not anything received the text — and then registered NO sinks. Six screens dispatch textInputRequests through a when(request.testTag) and all were working; the gate asserted a registration none performed, and every text input on every desktop went undrivable in one cut. Setup could not pass the YOU step; downstream adoption (CIRISAgent#1132) blocked. Same shape as the 0.5.196 supervisor nobody read: invariant right, wiring absent. rememberInputSinks() now sits on the line after each collector naming the tags its dispatch handles, and check_ui_drivable.py fails the build if a dispatched tag is undeclared — mutation-verified by removing one. /undrivable is stable and intended as a harness pre-flight.

rows.notes: THE MOBILE HALF OF CIRISClient#28. Android's TestAutomationServer logged 'Server started' immediately after Ktor's start(wait=false), which binds asynchronously — so the log reported readiness it had not checked, and a bind race read as an app fault: one /health answered and the next died with RemoteProtocolError, another night nothing within 90s. Readiness is now verified by actually connecting, and a failure to accept within 30s is logged as such. iOS ran a BLOCKING posix accept() on Dispatchers.Default and handed each accepted connection back to that same small pool, so the loop could starve the handlers it spawned — 'Server started' in the log and nothing answering for 120s. accept() now owns a dedicated Worker. AND THE SURFACE IS UNIFORM. handleInput answered success:true on mobile whether or not a field was listening — the 0.5.197 desktop bug, still live on the two platforms where automation is hardest — so a green setup step could have typed nothing. It now refuses with the same message. /tree carries canClick/canInput everywhere, and /undrivable and /state, previously desktop-only, are served by the shared handler on all five platforms; the pre-flight this repo tells harnesses to run now exists where they need it

rows.notes: THREE DEFECTS THE FIVE-PLATFORM GATE FOUND ONCE IT COULD FINALLY REACH MOBILE. #32: testableClickable kept the FIRST composition's onClick, because DisposableEffect was keyed on tag alone — so a programmatic click replayed a closure captured before the user typed, and Test Connection ran with an empty api key while the field visibly held one. Real mouse clicks were immune, which is why it survived manual testing. Desktop had fixed this with rememberUpdatedState and neither mobile platform inherited it; iOS was worse still, registering in the composable body with no DisposableEffect at all, so handlers re-registered every recomposition and never unregistered. All four variants now match desktop. #35: the iOS server read ONE recv() and parsed whatever arrived, so every POST body was empty and the decode error came back as the response — httpx writes headers and body separately. It now reads to Content-Length, finds the header terminator by byte offset rather than character index, and encodes error replies with the serializer instead of string paste, which is what made kotlinx's multi-line messages invalid JSON. #34: localizedString returned the raw KEY while isLoading, bypassing getString's whole cascade — current language, then English, then the key. English is loaded during init and isLoading starts true, so the fallback was usually already populated at the moment it was refusing to consult it; the first iOS screenshot the gate ever captured showed mobile.login_setup_complete_relogin to a user. The cascade now runs in every state AND THE CONTRACT #31 ASKED FOR. /input acknowledged work that had not happened: requestTextInput posts into a CONFLATING StateFlow and the handler returned success immediately, so three fields typed back-to-back returned three successes and the product answered “Password is required”. Even alone, success meant “posted”, never “changed”. It now waits for the flow to return to null — the apply signal every screen's dispatch already emits via clearTextInputRequest — before posting (serialising, so nothing is dropped) and again after, and a timeout is a FAILURE, because “I could not confirm this landed” is not success. No screen changed. ElementInfo now carries inputValue in /tree and /element, so a driver reads back what landed instead of inferring it from a screenshot; their read-back reports “unverifiable: element exposes no text” on every platform before this. startIfEnabled is idempotent on Android as well as iOS — reported for iOS, identical hole in the other: a second call bound-failed and then overwrote `instance` with the broken server, so a later stop() stopped the wrong object and left the working one running. NOT in this cut, and it is #31's fourth item: the .aar still ships no POM or .module metadata, which is why a Compose floor mismatch can only surface as a runtime NoSuchMethodError on a device. That is packaging work and wants its own change.
